To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a cryptic laminin peptide, STQ, binds to a cryptotrope in the beta1 chain of laminin-5 and that this peptide selectively inhibited tumor cell adhesion and invasion, angiogenesis, tumor cell proliferation, and experimental metastases in vivo.

we have isolated and characterized a synthetic peptide that recognizes a cryptic laminin peptide epitope that is exposed in vivo in malignant tumors but not in normal tissues and that targeting this epitope inhibits both tumor cell invasion and endothelial cell proliferation.
we identified a cryptic epitopes of laminin, and we demonstrated that targeting this epitope can inhibit angiogenesis and metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antiangiogenic and antimetastatic strategies for the treatment and prevention of human tumors.

the development of novel antiangiogenic and antitumor therapies by targeting cryptic epitopes in the extracellular matrix (matrix cryptic epitopes) and the development of new strategies for the prevention and treatment of cancer and angiogenesis-related diseases.

the identification and functional characterization of a cryptic extracellular epitope in laminins that is selectively expressed in malignant melanoma and that can be targeted for the development of new antiangiogenic/antimetastatic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the peptide STQ binds to a cryptically exposed epitope in laminins that is selectively exposed in malignant melanoma in mice and that the peptide STP inhibits tumor angiogenesis, tumor cell growth, and tumor cell metastatic spread.

the peptide STQ inhibits angiogenesis, tumor cell growth and metastasis in vivo and in vitro, and that this inhibitory effect is associated with a selective induction of cellular senescent and up-regulation of p27(KIP1).
the STQ peptide inhibits angiogenesis, tumor metastasis, and tumor growth by targeting a cryptic epitopes in laminin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel cryptic epitope of the extracellular matrix protein laminin and that targeting of this epitope inhibited angiogenesis and metastasis of malignant tumors.
we identified a cryptic laminin peptide that selectively targets the tumor microenvironment and induces a senescence response that inhibits tumor growth and metastasis.
we have isolated and characterized a novel synthetic peptide that targets an immobilized cryptic epitope on laminin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel cryptic epitope on laminin, which is exposed on tumor cells, but not on normal cells, and which is involved in the regulation of tumor cell invasion and metastasis.
targeting a specific cryptic epitope of the extracellular matrix can inhibit tumor growth and metastasis.
there are functionally relevant cryptotopes in the extracellular matrix and that they can be targeted to prevent tumor metastasis.
